newsitem.title: INDIA: India call eases, ends down, gilts end slightly up.
newsitem.headline: India call eases, ends down, gilts end slightly up.

text.p: Indian call money ended Wednesday at 7.25-7.5 percent, slightly down from opening quotes of 7.5-8.25 percent in quiet trade, dealers said.
They said most of the day' trade was between 7.5-8.0 percent in the morning and rates eased later as demand tapered off.
"Rates will drop below 7.0 percent tomorrow as most banks square up before the reporting Friday," said a dealer.
Banks report their fortnightly positions to the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) on Friday.
Dealers said prices of government securities were slightly up but trade was moderate. Most of the day's trade was in medium-tenure stocks, with maturities between 2000 and 2004.
Dealers said they expect trade to pick up once call money drops to around 5.0 percent.
"Many traders expect call money to ease to around 5.0 percent on Saturday when the new (reporting) fortnight begins," said a dealer. "Trade in securities will pick up then."
Among actively-traded stocks, the 12.14 percent 2000 stock traded on Wednesday between 104.37-104.41 rupees against Tuesday's close of 104.45.
The 11.55 percent 2002 improved to 101.69-101.75 against 101.55 while the 11.83 percent 2003 rose to 102.60-102.64 from 102.40. The 12.59 percent 2004 improved to 105.64-105.67 from 105.50.
Dealers said a certificate of deposit maturing in June 1998 was traded at a yield of 9.9 percent.
